desc:
A city has several bus lines. The array routes lists them: routes[i] holds the (distinct) stop numbers of line i, and every bus of line i drives around those stops in a loop forever, so you can get on or off at any of its stops at any time. A stop may belong to several lines.

You start at stop source and are not on a bus yet. Moving only by bus, find the smallest number of bus rides (boardings) needed to arrive at stop target. Staying on a line and riding through many stops counts as one ride; changing to another line counts as another. Return 0 if source == target, and -1 if the target cannot be reached.

routes = [[1,2,7], [3,6,7]], source = 1, target = 6
-> 2

Take line 0 from stop 1 to stop 7, then line 1 from stop 7 to stop 6.
constraints: 1 ≤ routes[i].length ≤ 100, the stops inside one line are distinct, and the total number of stops over all lines is at most 6,300
source and target need not appear in any line
hints: Think of what the BFS nodes should be. Modelling every stop as a node with an edge to every other stop on the same line has far too many edges.
The quantity you minimise is the number of lines used, so make each line a unit of the search: build a map from every stop to the lines that serve it.

BFS over stops, but process a line only once: when you pop stops of the current level, take every line serving them that has not been used yet, and all its stops form the next level. Count the levels.
editorial: Build lines_at[stop], the list of lines serving that stop. Run a level-by-level BFS where level k holds the stops reachable with exactly k rides. For the stops of the current level, take every line serving them that was not used before, mark it as used and look at all its stops: if one of them is the target, the answer is the current ride count; otherwise unseen stops form the next level.

Marking a line as used the first time it is met is the key to efficiency: each line's stop list is scanned only once, so the total work is O(total number of stops). Using the first level where the target appears is correct because BFS finds the fewest rides. A source equal to the target needs no ride, and a source or target that no line serves makes the answer -1.
time: O(S) where S is the total number of stops over all lines
